definition_en: forbidden by law or by official rules, and punishable if done
core_image: 大楼门口一块被红笔划掉的车位牌，写着此处禁止停车
scene: 市中心的巷口立着一块新做的牌子。Parking there is illegal after eight in the evening, so drivers keep moving past it.
sceneCN: 这里 illegal 指「非法的、违法的」（第 1 个义项：法律明令禁止），句意是晚上八点后在那里停车属违法，于是司机们一路开过去。画面里有巷口、新牌子和不肯停下的车。

senses.title: Forbidden by law
senses.definition: against the law and punishable by the courts
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律、会被法院处罚的
senses.example: It is illegal to sell alcohol to children.
senses.exampleCN: 向儿童出售酒类是违法的。
senses.why: The prefix in- here works as a pure negative, so the word simply says that a thing does not fall inside the law.
senses.whyCN: 这里的前缀表否定，词义就是「这件事不在法律许可的范围之内」。

senses.title: Against the rules of a sport or game
senses.definition: not allowed by the rules of a game or competition
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则的
senses.example: The referee ruled that the tackle was illegal.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判判定这次抢球属于犯规。
senses.why: Sport has its own rule book, and since the word points at any codified rule, it slid easily from courts of law to fields of play.
senses.whyCN: 体育有自己的规则册，而这个词指向一切成文规则，于是自然从法庭滑到了球场。

senses.title: Not officially approved

senses.definitionCN: 未获官方许可而做的，尤指建筑或经营
senses.example: An illegal extension was built onto the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 房子后面加建了一间未经批准的屋子。
senses.why: Modern life adds licences and permits to law, and anything done outside them borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活给法律添上执照与许可，凡在许可之外做的事也借用同一个词。

intro.en: Illegal joins a Latin negative prefix to the Latin word for law; it entered English through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: illegal 由拉丁语否定前缀与拉丁语「法律」一词合成，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Lex, legis meant law, whether a statute or a binding custom of the community.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex、属格 legis 意为「法律」，既指成文法，也指共同体约束性的习俗。

items.en: Legalis described what belonged to law and was lawful, a word already carrying a clear yes or no.
items.cn: legalis 形容「属于法律的、合法的」，本身已带有明确的是非判断。

items.en: Adding the negative in-, scribes formed illegals to name what fell outside the law.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 后，抄写者们造出 illegals，用来指法律之外的事。

items.en: French carried the form as illegal, and its legal clerks used it constantly in court records.
items.cn: 法语以 illegal 的形式承下此词，司法文书里频繁使用。

items.en: English took it up in the sixteenth century and broadened it to rules of sports, trades and building.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪收入该词，并把适用范围扩展到体育规则、行业与建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the il- family born from the same negative prefix; the near-meaning group collects other strong words for what is not allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由否定前缀 il- 生成的家族词；近义组收其他表示「不被允许」的强词。

entries.definition: Not following reason; it shares the same il- prefix and the same negative force.
entries.definitionCN: 不合逻辑的；共用同一个 il- 否定前缀与否定意味。

entries.definition: Impossible to read, built with the same prefix but applied to writing.
entries.definitionCN: 难以辨认的，前缀相同但用于书写。

entries.definition: Not allowed or not valid, a close cousin that adds the idea of legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 不正当的、无效的，多了一层「正当性」的意思。

entries.definition: Not permitted by law, the plainest native synonym of illegal.
entries.definitionCN: 不合法的，是 illegal 最直白的同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to crime; stronger, since it names punishable wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪的；语气更重，因为它直接指向应受刑罚的恶行。

entries.definition: Not allowed by someone in authority, often a household or a school.
entries.definitionCN: 被禁止的，多用于当权者的规定，如家中或校内。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the Latin law root and the loud negative prefix to fix the spelling and the meaning together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借拉丁语「法律」词根与显眼的否定前缀，把拼写与词义一起钉住。

normal.en: il- is a negative prefix, and legal is law, so illegal is literally not legal.
normal.cn: il- 是否定前缀，legal 是法律上的，所以 illegal 字面上就是「不合法」。

normal.en: The double l is the trick of spelling: the in- of negation folds into the l of legal.
normal.cn: 拼写难点在双 l：否定的 in- 在 l 前同化成 il-。

normal.en: The same il- hides in illogical and illegible, so any il- word is a no.
normal.cn: 同一个 il- 也藏在 illogical 与 illegible 里，凡以 il- 开头都是「不」。

normal.en: Say it with the stress on the second beat: il-LEE-gal, like LEAR in legal.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二拍：il-LEE-gal，与 legal 里的 LE- 呼应。

normal.en: Remember the traffic sign with the red circle and a slash: that circle is illegal in picture form.
normal.cn: 记住交通牌上带斜杠的红圈：那个圈就是 illegal 的图解。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in chalk around the law; everything outside the line is not banned by nature, only by that line.
abstract.cn: 想象用粉笔绕法律画了一圈：圈外的事本身并非天理不容，只是被那条线挡住。

abstract.en: The word never denies that an act happens; it only reports that the law refuses to approve of it.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不否认事情真的发生了，只说法律不肯点头。

abstract.en: A prefix as small as two letters can turn a permission into a prohibition, which shows how thin the line between yes and no is.
abstract.cn: 两个字母的前缀就能把允许翻成禁止，由此可见允与禁之间的界线有多薄。

examples.en: It is illegal to drive without a licence.
examples.cn: 无证驾驶是违法的。

examples.en: The factory was fined for illegal waste dumping.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因非法倾倒废物被罚款。

examples.en: Officials promised to close the illegal market within a week.
examples.cn: 官员承诺一周内取缔这个非法市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: il 不 + legal 合法的——不合法的，字面就是「不合法」

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）「法律」→ legalis「合法的」，加否定前缀 in-（在 l 前同化为 il-）成 illegals，经古法语 illegal 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: what the law forbids, what the rules of a game forbid, and what lacks official approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：法律禁止的、比赛规则禁止的，以及缺少官方批准的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line drawn around the law, with everything beyond it closed off.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕法律画出一道红线，线外之事全部封闭。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: selling to children or driving unlicensed is against statute.
branches.cn: 法律线：向儿童售酒、无照驾驶都触犯法条。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: a rough tackle is illegal under the rules of football.
branches.cn: 球场线：足球里粗野抢球按规则属于犯规。

branches.en: THE PERMIT LINE: an extension built without papers is illegal even if nobody complains.
branches.cn: 许可线：没有手续的加建，即使无人投诉也属违建。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: both senses need an authority to say no.
branches.cn: 裁决线：两种用法都需要一个权威来判定「不行」。

branches.en: THE PAPER LINE: licences and statutes are the documents the word quietly points at.
branches.cn: 文书线：执照与法规正是这个词默默指向的纸面依据。

intro.en: Illegal is a clean prefix-plus-root pattern: a Latin negative, a Latin law root, and English endings built on both.
intro.cn: illegal 是干净的前缀加词根结构：拉丁语否定前缀、拉丁语法律词根，以及在这两者上长出的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The negative in- and the law root lex are both attested in Latin, and the assimilation of n to l is a regular sound change.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀 in- 与法律词根 lex 在拉丁语中都有文献，n 同化为 l 是规律性的语音变化。

items.example: The same prefix appears in illogical.
items.exampleCN: 同一个前缀也见于 illogical。

items.example: The contract is legal and binding.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同合法且具约束力。

items.example: Illegal parking blocks the fire lane.
items.exampleCN: 违章停车堵住了消防通道。

items.example: He parked illegally outside the school.
items.exampleCN: 他把车违法停在了学校门外。

items.meaning: the state of being against law
items.example: The court examined the illegality of the order.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了这道命令的违法性。

items.example: She had a legitimate reason to complain.
Unlawful entry carries a heavy fine.

latinEntries.meaning: a proposer or maker of laws

definition_en: the state of being unwell, or a particular disease that a person has
core_image: 床头柜上摊开的温水和几板药片，窗帘半掩着
scene: 孩子连着两晚发烧，母亲请了假守在家里。The illness lasted a week, so the whole family learned to move quietly around the sickroom.
sceneCN: 这里 illness 指「疾病、生病」（第 1 个义项：身体不健康的状态），句意是这场病持续了一周，全家人学会了在病床边轻手轻脚。画面里有温水、药片和半掩的窗帘。

senses.title: The state of being unwell
senses.definition: the condition of being in poor health over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内身体健康不佳的状况
senses.example: His illness kept him away from work for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病让他一个月没能上班。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective ill into an abstract state, so the word names a condition rather than a single symptom.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 ill 变成抽象状态，因此这个词指的是一段处境，而非单个症状。

senses.title: A particular disease
senses.definition: a specific sickness with a name, such as measles or diabetes
senses.definitionCN: 有名称的某种具体病症，如麻疹或糖尿病
senses.example: She suffers from a rare blood illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她患有一种罕见的血液病。
senses.why: Once people began diagnosing in detail, the state word was reused for each named disease the doctors could identify.
senses.whyCN: 当诊断细化之后，这个表示状态的词就被借去指医生能一一命名的病症。

senses.title: A period of sickness
senses.definition: a stretch of time during which someone is ill
senses.definitionCN: 一个人患病的这段时间
senses.example: During his illness the neighbours brought meals every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 在他患病期间，邻居们每晚都送来饭菜。
senses.why: English often measures states by their duration, and so the word is used for the span as well as the condition.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用时长来衡量状态，于是这个词既指病情，也指那一整段时间。

intro.en: Illness is an Old Norse word dressed with an English ending: ill came from the north and -ness is native.
intro.cn: illness 是古诺斯语词根加英语词尾：ill 来自北方，-ness 是本土成分。

items.en: The Scandinavian adjective illr meant bad or evil, covering both harm and moral wrong.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚语形容词 illr 意为「坏的、恶的」，兼指伤害与道德之恶。

items.en: English already had -nes, a suffix that turned adjectives into names for their states.
items.cn: 英语早已有 -nes 这一词尾，能把形容词变成表示状态的抽象名词。

items.en: After the Norse settlers, ill settled into English and gradually narrowed towards poor health.
items.cn: 北欧移民进入英格兰后，ill 扎根英语，词义逐渐收窄到健康不佳。

items.en: Combining ill with -ness gave illness, first as wickedness and later as sickness.
items.cn: ill 与 -ness 结合成 illness，最初表「邪恶」，后来转为「疾病」。

items.en: Medical writing fixed illness as the standard abstract noun for poor health and named diseases.
items.cn: 医学写作把 illness 固定为表示不健康与具体病症的标准抽象名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -ness words built on short adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers words for sickness itself.
note.cn: 形近组收其他由短形容词加 -ness 构成的词；近义组收表示疾病本身的词。

entries.definition: The state of being weak, made the same way from a short adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱、弱点，构成方式相同。

entries.definition: The state of being sad, another abstract noun on -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤，又一个 -ness 抽象名词。

entries.definition: The state of doing nothing, close in shape to illness.
entries.definitionCN: 闲散、无所事事，形状与 illness 相近。

entries.definition: A medical condition with identifiable signs, often more clinical than illness.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确体征的疾病，比 illness 更偏医学。

entries.definition: The state of being sick, or vomiting; plainer and often physical.
entries.definitionCN: 生病、恶心呕吐；更口语，也常指生理反应。

entries.definition: A minor illness that keeps troubling someone over time.
entries.definitionCN: 常年缠人的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the suffix -ness, the Norse origin, and the everyday details of being sick in bed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用上 -ness 词尾、北欧来源以及卧病在床的日常细节。

normal.en: ill is the adjective, -ness makes the state, so illness is the condition of being ill.
normal.cn: ill 是形容词，-ness 把状态名词化，illness 就是「生病这件事」。

normal.en: Spell it with double l, just as in ill, plus ness: illness, four letters then four.
normal.cn: 拼写用双 l，与 ill 一致，再加 ness：前半四个字母，后半也是四个。

normal.en: The word came from the north with the Vikings, so the l's are not silent.
normal.cn: 这个词随北欧人从北方而来，其中的 l 要发出来。

normal.en: Only two syllables, stress the first: ILL-ness.
normal.cn: 只有两个音节，重音在前：ILL-ness。

normal.en: Think of a sick note on an office desk: the paper names an illness, not a person.
normal.cn: 想想办公桌上的一张病假条：纸上写的是病名，不是人名。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning of the root was evil, not sickness, which shows how a moral word can drift into medicine.
abstract.cn: 这个词根最古老的意思是「恶」而非「病」，可见道德词如何漂进医学。

abstract.en: A suffix of four letters turns a passing adjective into a whole season of life, which is why illness feels longer than ill.
abstract.cn: 四个字母的词尾把一时的形容词变成人生的一整段，所以 illness 听起来比 ill 更长。

abstract.en: The word describes a condition, never a blame; it holds a person without judging one.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述的是处境，从不追究过错；它承载一个人，却不评判一个人。

examples.en: She took three days off because of illness.
examples.cn: 她因病请了三天假。

examples.en: Mental illness deserves the same care as physical illness.
examples.cn: 精神疾病应当得到与身体疾病同样的关怀。

examples.en: He never spoke about his long illness at work.
examples.cn: 他在单位从不谈自己长期的病。

dict_mnemonic.text: ill 生病的 + ness 状态名词尾——生病的状态，即疾病

root: 古诺斯语 illr「坏的、恶的」→ 中古英语 ill「不佳、有病」，加本土词尾 -nes（今 -ness）构成表示状态的抽象名词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the state of poor health, a named disease, and the period it lasts.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：健康不佳的状态、有名称的具体疾病，以及疾病持续的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of water and tablets on a bedside table with the curtain half drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头柜上一杯水和几板药片，窗帘半掩。

branches.en: THE STATE LINE: the word names a stretch of poor health, not one symptom.
branches.cn: 状态线：这个词指一段时间的不健康，而非单个症状。

branches.en: THE DIAGNOSIS LINE: doctors attach the word to named diseases.
branches.cn: 诊断线：医生把这个词挂到有名字的病症上。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: during his illness marks a period with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 日历线：患病期间标记出一段有始有终的时间。

branches.en: THE BED LINE: rest, medicine and quiet neighbours all belong to it.
branches.cn: 病床线：休息、药物与轻声的邻居都属于它。

branches.en: THE WORK LINE: a sick note certifies illness so the office accepts it.
branches.cn: 单位线：病假条为 illness 作证，单位才会认可。

intro.en: Illness is a short Norse adjective plus a native abstract suffix, one of the most ordinary patterns in English.
intro.cn: illness 是一个简短的北欧形容词加本土抽象词尾，属于英语最普通的构词方式。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin: the adjective travelled from Old Norse and the suffix is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这两部分都不来自拉丁语：形容词来自古诺斯语，词尾属日耳曼语。

items.example: He felt ill after the long journey.
items.exampleCN: 长途旅行后他觉得不适。

items.example: Kindness and darkness use it too.
items.exampleCN: kindness 与 darkness 也用这个词尾。

items.example: He had several illnesses as a child.

items.exampleCN: 她抱病的父亲需要照料。

definition_zh: 阐明；说明；演示；给（书）加插图
definition_en: to make something clear by giving examples or pictures, or to add pictures to a book
core_image: 黑板上被老师用红粉笔圈出的一幅示意图
scene: 物理老师讲浮力时先放下教材，转身在黑板上画了一条船。She used two arrows to illustrate how the water pushed the hull upward.
sceneCN: 这里 illustrate 是「阐明、说明」（第 1 个义项：用例子或图示把道理讲清），句意是她用两个箭头说明水如何把船体托起。画面里有黑板、红粉笔和一艘简笔画的船。

pos.zh: 动词：阐明、说明；给书加插图

senses.title: To make an idea clear
senses.definition: to explain something by giving examples or by showing how it works
senses.definitionCN: 用例子或演示来说明某事
senses.example: Let me illustrate the rule with a simple case.
senses.exampleCN: 让我用个简单的例子说明这条规则。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to light up, and an example does exactly that for an abstract idea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根本是「照亮」，而例子对抽象观念所做的正是照亮。

senses.title: To add pictures to a text
senses.definition: to supply drawings or photographs for a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 为书籍或杂志提供插图或照片
senses.example: A young artist illustrated the whole storybook.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻画家为整本故事书画了插图。
senses.why: Pictures make a text bright and easy to grasp, so the same verb was extended from words to images.
senses.whyCN: 图画使文字明朗易懂，于是同一个动词从说明扩展到配图。

senses.title: To be an example of
senses.definition: to serve as a clear instance that shows a general fact
senses.definitionCN: 作为能说明普遍事实的明确例子
senses.example: His career illustrates how talent and luck combine.
senses.exampleCN: 他的经历说明了天赋与运气如何结合。
senses.why: When a case makes a truth visible, English lets the case itself become the subject and light up the claim.
senses.whyCN: 当一个事例让道理显现时，英语就让这个事例作主语，替主张打光。

intro.en: Illustrate goes back to a Latin verb for lighting up, and that image of light still sits inside the word.
intro.cn: illustrate 可追溯到一个意为「照亮」的拉丁动词，光的意象至今留在词里。

items.en: Lustrare meant to light up or make bright, and was used of light striking a dark place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lustrare 意为照亮、使明亮，常指光照进暗处。

items.en: Illustrare strengthened it: to throw light on, and figuratively to make clear to the mind.
items.cn: illustrare 加强此义：把光照上去，引申为使心中明白。

items.en: Church writers used illustrare of famous men whose deeds lit up their age.
items.cn: 教会作家用 illustrare 形容功业照亮时代的著名人物。

items.en: English borrowed it as illustren, first meaning to enlighten or bring honour.
items.cn: 英语以 illustren 借入，最初意为启迪或增光。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the printing trade made to add pictures the everyday meaning.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，印刷业让「加插图」成了最日常的词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for making things clear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁家族里的词；近义组收其他表示讲清楚的动词。

entries.definition: A picture or example that lights up a point.
entries.definitionCN: 插图或例证，用来把观点照亮。

entries.definition: Famous and admired, literally shining with light.
entries.definitionCN: 著名的、辉煌的，字面就是「发光」。

entries.definition: A soft shine on a surface, from the same light word.
entries.definitionCN: 表面的柔和光泽，同出光明一词。

entries.definition: To make something plain by giving reasons; broader than illustrate.
entries.definitionCN: 通过讲道理把事情说清楚，范围比 illustrate 更广。

entries.definition: To show clearly by doing or by proof.
entries.definitionCN: 通过演示或证据明确展示。

entries.definition: To remove confusion from a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 消除说法中的含混之处。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the light inside illustrare to pictures, examples and clear blackboard arrows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 illustrare 里的「光」连到插图、例子与黑板上清晰的箭头。

normal.en: The Latin root means light: to illustrate is to shine a lamp on an idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为光：illustrate 就是给一个想法打灯。

normal.en: The ill- here is not a negative prefix, so do not read it as not legal.
normal.cn: 这里的 ill- 不是否定前缀，别误读成「不合法」。

normal.en: The stress falls in the middle: il-LUS-trate.
normal.cn: 重音在中间：il-LUS-trate。

normal.en: -ate marks a verb, and its relatives are all nouns or adjectives of light and picture.
normal.cn: -ate 标示动词，它的同族词都与光和图画相关。

normal.en: A book with pictures is an illustrated book, so the verb keeps a footprint on every page.
normal.cn: 带图的书叫 illustrated book，这个动词在每一页上都留下脚印。

abstract.en: Explaining and drawing are two limbs of one act: both pull an invisible thought into the visible world.
abstract.cn: 讲解与绘图是同一动作的两条胳膊：都把看不见的想法拉进可见世界。

abstract.en: The word trusts the example more than the rule, because a lit case teaches faster than a definition.
abstract.cn: 这个词更信例子而非规则，因为被照亮的事例比定义教得快。

abstract.en: A single illustration can do what a whole paragraph cannot, which is why the picture stayed inside the verb.
abstract.cn: 一幅插图能做出整段文字做不到的事，所以图画一直住在动词里。

examples.en: The teacher illustrated the idea with a simple diagram.
examples.cn: 老师用一张简图说明了这个概念。

examples.en: This case clearly illustrates why the rules are needed.
examples.cn: 这个案例清楚说明了为什么需要这些规则。

examples.en: She has illustrated more than thirty children's books.
examples.cn: 她为三十多本童书绘制过插图。

dict_mnemonic.text: illustr 光（拉丁语「照亮」）+ ate 动词——把光照到想法上，就是阐明；配图也是照亮

root: 拉丁语 lustrare「照亮」→ illustrare「照亮、使明白」，中世纪拉丁语引申为增光，中古英语借入为 illustren，近代定形 illustrate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: to make an idea clear, to add pictures to a text, and to serve as a telling example.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：讲清一个观点、给文字配图，以及本身成为有力的例证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red chalk circle on a blackboard diagram, lighting up how a boat floats.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板示意图上被红粉笔圈出的一处，照亮船为什么浮。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM LINE: an example illuminates an abstract rule.
branches.cn: 课堂线：一个例子照亮一条抽象规则。

branches.en: THE PRINT LINE: drawings light up a page of text.
branches.cn: 印刷线：图画照亮一整页文字。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE LINE: a career or a case can be the example itself.
branches.cn: 证据线：一段经历或一个案例本身就充当例证。

branches.en: THE LIGHT LINE: all three keep the original image of throwing light.
branches.cn: 光之线：三个义项都保留「投光」的原意象。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: in essays the verb introduces proof, not decoration.
branches.cn: 论证线：在议论文里这个词引出的是证据，不是装饰。

intro.en: Illustrate is a Latin verb taken over almost whole, with English endings and a large family of relatives.
intro.cn: illustrate 几乎是整体搬来的拉丁动词，只换英语词尾，并带出一大串同族词。

latinIntro.en: The light root lustr- is recorded in Latin, and the prefix il- here is the preposition in-, not a negative.
latinIntro.cn: 表示光的词根 lustr- 有拉丁文献，这里的前缀 il- 是介词 in- 的变形，并非否定。

items.example: The root also hides in lustre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也藏在 lustre 里。

items.example: Create and activate behave the same way.
items.exampleCN: create 与 activate 也一样。
她的经历说明了这种危险。

items.meaning: past form or describing a book with pictures
items.meaningCN: 过去式，或形容配有插图的书

items.exampleCN: 这些数字只是示意性的。

items.example: The illustrator signed the first page.
items.exampleCN: 插画家在第一页签了名。

latinEntries.meaning: to light up, to make bright

definition_en: a picture of someone or something, or the idea that people have of a person or a company
core_image: 橱窗里一张被灯光打亮的人物海报
scene: 地铁通道的灯箱一夜之间全换了内容。The image of a smiling farmer held the same pose on every panel, so commuters looked twice.
sceneCN: 这里 image 是「影像、图像」（第 1 个义项：人或物的画面），句意是一位微笑农夫的照片在每个灯箱上都保持同一姿势，乘客忍不住多看两眼。画面里有地铁通道和发亮的灯箱。

pos.zh: 名词：形象、影像、图像；印象

senses.title: A picture of something
senses.definition: a picture produced by a camera, a screen or a mirror
senses.definitionCN: 由相机、屏幕或镜子形成的画面
senses.example: The screen showed a sharp image of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上出现了清晰的月球影像。
senses.why: The word entered English as a name for a copy of a thing, a shape standing in for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，本是指某物的复制之形，即代替实物存在的那个样子。

senses.title: The idea people have of someone
senses.definition: the impression that a person or organisation gives to the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或机构给公众留下的总体观感
senses.example: The firm hired a designer to rebuild its image.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘请设计师重塑形象。
senses.why: The picture in public minds is treated as if it were a picture on a wall, so the same noun serves for fame and reputation.
senses.whyCN: 公众心中的那幅画被当成挂在墙上的画，于是同一个名词也用来指声望与口碑。

senses.title: A word picture in art and poetry
senses.definition: a description or figure of speech that makes readers see something
senses.definitionCN: 让读者眼前浮现画面的描写或修辞
senses.example: The poem opens with an image of rain on an empty road.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗以空荡路上下雨的意象开篇。
senses.why: Literature borrows the visual word because a good phrase paints a picture inside the reader.
senses.whyCN: 文学借用这个视觉词，因为一句好话能在读者心里画出图来。

intro.en: Image comes from a Latin word for a likeness or a statue, and it still keeps that sense of a shape standing for something.
intro.cn: image 来自拉丁语中表示「相似之物、雕像」的词，至今仍保留「以形代物」的含义。

items.en: Imago was a likeness, whether a carved statue or the picture of a face.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指相像之物，既可为雕像，也可为面容的图画。

items.en: Imaginem was the accusative form most often met in texts, and it gave the word to later languages.
items.cn: 宾格形式 imaginem 在文献中最常见，后来的语言正是从这里取词。

items.en: French shortened it to image, still meaning a copy or a figure.
items.cn: 法语把它缩为 image，仍指复制之形或人物形象。

items.en: English adopted the French form and used it for statues, paintings and pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 英语沿用此形，用来指雕像、绘画以及心中的画面。

items.en: Photography and later television widened it to any picture made by light or by a screen.
items.cn: 摄影与后来的电视把它扩展到一切由光或屏幕生成的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same imag- root; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns for pictures.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 imag- 为词根的词；近义组收其他表示画面的名词。

entries.definition: To form a picture in the mind, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中构出画面，同一词根。

entries.definition: Images as a group, especially in art or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 图像或意象的集合，尤用于艺术与文学。

entries.definition: A copy of something, built on a similar pattern though not the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 仿制品，构词形式相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: A painting, drawing or photograph, the plainest everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画、图画或照片，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: An image made by light on film or a sensor.
entries.definitionCN: 由光线落在胶片或传感器上形成的影像。

entries.definition: The opinion others hold of a person, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 他人对某人的评价，与第二个义项相近。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the Latin statue imago to screens, mirrors and public faces.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语的雕像 imago 连到屏幕、镜子和公众面孔上。

normal.en: Drop the final e and you get imag-, the root that also grows imagine and imagery.
normal.cn: 去掉词尾的 e 得到 imag-，这个词根还长出 imagine 与 imagery。

normal.en: Six letters, stress the first: IM-age.
normal.cn: 六个字母，重音在前：IM-age。

normal.en: Soft g at the end, so it rhymes with village, not with cage.
normal.cn: 结尾的 g 发软音，与 village 押韵，而不与 cage 同音。

normal.en: A mirror gives a mirror image, and a screen gives a digital image; the word is always a copy.
normal.cn: 镜子给出镜像，屏幕给出数字图像；这个词始终是复制品。

normal.en: Companies worry about their image just as cameras worry about theirs: both are pictures seen by others.
normal.cn: 公司操心形象，正如镜头操心成像：都是别人看见的那幅画。

abstract.en: An image is never the thing itself; it is the thing seen from outside, frozen long enough to be looked at.
abstract.cn: 图像从不是事物本身，而是事物从外部被看见、并被冻住足够久以供注视的样子。

abstract.en: The word holds both a mirror and a reputation, because people build a picture of you and then live beside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着一面镜子和一份名声，因为人们先为你画像，再与那幅画同住。

abstract.en: Every picture is a small promise that a thing can be held still, and every failure of that promise disappoints us.
abstract.cn: 每幅画都是一个小承诺：事物可以被定住；这个承诺一旦落空，我们就会失望。

examples.en: The telescope sent back clear images of the planet.
examples.cn: 望远镜传回了这颗行星的清晰图像。

examples.en: Her public image as a strict judge is not quite fair.
examples.cn: 她作为严苛法官的公众形象并不太公允。

examples.en: He tried to improve the image of the brand after the scandal.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后他设法改善这个品牌的形象。

dict_mnemonic.text: imag 像（拉丁语「雕像、形貌」）+ e——照出来的样子，即影像；别人心中的样子，即形象

root: 拉丁语 imago（宾格 imaginem）「相似之物、雕像」，经古法语 image 进入英语，现代扩展到摄影图像与公众形象。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a visible picture, the picture held in public opinion, and a word picture in art.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：可见的画面、舆论中持有的印象，以及文学艺术中语言绘出的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit poster of a face repeated along a subway wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：地铁墙上被灯照亮、反复出现的同一张面孔。

branches.en: THE LENS LINE: cameras, screens and mirrors all produce images.
branches.cn: 镜头线：相机、屏幕与镜子都在产生图像。

branches.en: THE BRAND LINE: a company's image is its face in public.
branches.cn: 品牌线：公司的形象就是它在公众面前的脸。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: poets build images out of plain words.
branches.cn: 纸页线：诗人用朴素的词造出意象。

branches.en: THE COPY LINE: both are pictures standing in for something else.
branches.cn: 复制线：两者都是以画代物的复制。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: whether on glass or in lines of verse, the target is the eye.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：无论印在玻璃上还是写在诗句里，目标都是眼睛。

intro.en: Image is a Latin root with a light English ending; its family spreads across verbs, adjectives and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: image 是拉丁语词根加轻巧的英语词尾，其家族遍及动词、形容词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Imago and its stem imagin- are recorded in classical Latin, so the family rests on solid ground.
latinIntro.cn: imago 及其词干 imagin- 在古典拉丁语中都有文献，这个家族根基扎实。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 imagery 中。

items.example: The film is full of strong images.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片充满强烈的意象。
她的想象力填补了空白。

items.example: The poem's imagery is all water.

items.exampleCN: 他们试了所有想得到的方法。

definition_en: the ability to form pictures and ideas in the mind, including things that are not actually present
core_image: 深夜书桌上散开的草图，窗外的云被画成了飞鱼
scene: 作文题只有一行字，纸上却很快铺满了东西。Her imagination turned a bare classroom into a ship, and the whole class began to steer it.
sceneCN: 这里 imagination 指「想象力」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面的能力），句意是她的想象把空荡荡的教室变成一艘船，全班开始一起掌舵。画面里有只写一行字的作文题和慢慢填满的纸。

pos.zh: 名词：想象力、想象、创造力

senses.title: The power to form pictures
senses.definition: the ability to create images and situations in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中造出画面与情境的能力
senses.example: Children need imagination more than they need toys.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要想象力胜过需要玩具。
senses.why: The -ation ending names the faculty itself, so the word points to an ability rather than to a single picture.
senses.whyCN: -ation 词尾命名的是能力本身，因此这个词指向一种本领，而非某一幅画面。

senses.title: Something invented in the mind
senses.definition: a product of the mind that has no basis in fact
senses.definitionCN: 头脑造出、并无事实依据之物
senses.example: The monster was pure imagination, he admitted later.
senses.exampleCN: 他后来承认那怪物纯属想象。
senses.why: A faculty word easily slides into the thing the faculty produces, just as writing means both skill and text.
senses.whyCN: 表示能力的词很容易滑向它所产出之物，正如 writing 既指写作技能又指文字。

senses.title: Creative power in art or science
senses.definition: the inventive power behind new designs, stories or theories
senses.definitionCN: 催生新设计、新故事或新理论的创造能力
senses.example: The vaccine grew from years of scientific imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗源自多年科学上的创造力。
senses.why: Inventing and picturing rely on the same act of seeing what is not there, so the word covers both art and discovery.
senses.whyCN: 发明与想象都依赖同一个动作——看见尚不存在之物，于是这个词兼指艺术与发现。

intro.en: Imagination is the Latin noun built on imaginari, to picture to oneself, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: imagination 建立在拉丁语 imaginari（在心中构想）之上的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture something to oneself, active mental seeing rather than mere copying.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imaginari 意为在心头构想某物，是主动的心里观想，而非单纯复制。

items.en: Imaginatio named the faculty that holds such pictures, discussed at length by medieval scholars.
items.cn: imaginatio 命名持有这些画面的能力，中世纪学者对此多有讨论。

items.en: French used imagination for the mind's picturing power, both serious and playful.
items.cn: 法语用 imagination 指心智造图之力，严肃与游戏皆可。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fourteenth century, first in medicine and philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，最初见于医学与哲学。

items.en: Romantic writers raised imagination to a creative force, and education took it as a core skill.
items.cn: 浪漫主义作家把想象提升为创造之力，教育也把它视作核心素养。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's other noun-like forms; the near-meaning group gathers powers of the mind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的其他名词性形式；近义组收其他表示心智力气的词。

entries.definition: Pictures in art or writing, near in shape but not the faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术或文学中的意象，形状相近但并非能力。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind, an adjective where this word is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中的：本词是名词，它是形容词。

entries.definition: Full of imagination, the adjective built on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 富有想象力的，与本词同基的形容词。

entries.definition: The power to make new things, closer to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 创造新事物的能力，更接近第三个义项。

entries.definition: A scene invented in the mind, often pleasant and impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 脑中虚构的情景，常是愉悦而不可能发生的。

entries.definition: The making of something new, or something made up.
entries.definitionCN: 造出新事物，也可指编造之物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks place the -ation heavy ending beside the lighter verb and adjective forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把沉重的 -ation 词尾与较轻盈的动词、形容词形式并排放。

normal.en: Long words often mirror long ability: five syllables for a power that never runs short.
normal.cn: 长词常对应绵长的能力：五个音节，配一种用不完的本事。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: i-ma-gi-NA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音落在第四音节：i-ma-gi-NA-tion。

normal.en: Its verb is imagine and its adjective imaginative; the ending changes the word's role.
normal.cn: 动词是 imagine，形容词是 imaginative，词尾改变的是词的职务。

normal.en: The root imag- sits inside image, so the power is always about making pictures.
normal.cn: 词根 imag- 就在 image 里，这种能力始终与造画面有关。

normal.en: Say beyond imagination and you name a limit you cannot measure.
normal.cn: 说「超乎想象」，你命名的是一条量不出的界线。

abstract.en: Imagination is not the opposite of knowledge; it is knowledge reaching for what does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 想象并不是知识的反面，而是知识伸手去够还不存在的东西。

abstract.en: A child with a stick and a good imagination owns a horse, a sword and a whole kingdom.
abstract.cn: 一个拿着棍子、想象丰沛的孩子，同时拥有一匹马、一把剑和整个王国。

abstract.en: The word describes a power that grows when used and withers when denied, unlike almost every other faculty.
abstract.cn: 这种能力越用越强、越禁越枯，几乎与所有其他本领都不同。

examples.en: The story caught the imagination of readers everywhere.
examples.cn: 这个故事激发了各地读者的想象。

examples.en: She has a vivid imagination and draws monsters every day.
examples.cn: 她想象力丰富，每天都画怪物。

examples.en: Solving the problem required imagination as much as knowledge.
examples.cn: 解决这个问题既需要知识，也同样需要想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: imagine 想象 + ation 名词尾——想象的能力，即想象力

root: 拉丁语 imaginari「在心中构想」（词干 imagin-）→ imaginatio，经古法语 imagination 进入英语，近代由文学与教育学定为「想象力」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the power to picture, the products of that power, and its creative force in art and science.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：造画面的能力、这种能力的产物，以及它在艺术与科学中的创造力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sketch pads under a lamp, with clouds redrawn as flying fish.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下摊开的草图本，云被改画成飞鱼。

branches.en: THE FACULTY LINE: the word names a lasting capacity of the mind.
branches.cn: 能力线：这个词命名心智中一种持久的本领。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT LINE: monsters and kingdoms are its output.
branches.cn: 产物线：怪物与王国都是它的产物。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE LINE: designs and theories grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 创造线：设计与理论也从同一根部长出来。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: teachers value it alongside memory and logic.
branches.cn: 学校线：教师把它与记忆、逻辑并列看待。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY LINE: the same power gives both the picture and the fake.
branches.cn: 边界线：同一种能力既给出画面，也给出假象。

intro.en: Imagination is the heaviest member of the image family, built with the Latin noun ending -atio.
intro.cn: imagination 是 image 家族里最重的一员，用拉丁语名词词尾 -atio 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both imaginatio and its verb imaginari are recorded in Latin prose, so no reconstruction is needed.
latinIntro.cn: imaginatio 及其动词 imaginari 在拉丁语散文中均有记录，无需构拟。

items.exampleCN: image 与 imagery 共用此词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或能力的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: 想象力造出了整台机器。
他们的想象各走各的路。

items.example: Imagine a city with no cars.
items.exampleCN: 想象一座没有汽车的城市。
那是个富有想象力的设计。

items.example: The novel is rich in imagery.

definition_en: to form a picture of something in the mind, or to suppose that something is true
core_image: 闭上眼伸手在空中画出形状的那个人
scene: 培训师让全员先放下笔。Close your eyes and imagine the shop on a busy Saturday, she said, then write what the door sounds like.
sceneCN: 这里 imagine 是「想象、设想」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面），句意是她让大家闭上眼想象周六热闹的店铺，再写下门的声音。画面里有放下笔的学员和空中画出的形状。

pos.zh: 动词：想象、设想；猜想、料想

senses.title: To form a picture in the mind
senses.definition: to create an idea or image of something in your thinking
senses.definitionCN: 在思维中造出某物的意念或画面
senses.example: Imagine standing on that bridge at sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 想象一下日出时站在那座桥上。
senses.why: The verb is the action version of the picture word, so it names the work of building an inner image on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是「画面」一词的动作版，指有意在内部造出图像的过程。

senses.title: To suppose or guess
senses.definition: to think that something is probably true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在无证据的情况下认为某事大概为真
senses.example: I imagine he is still waiting at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜他还在车站等着。
senses.why: When we cannot see, we build a picture and treat it as the truth, and the same verb covers that guess.
senses.whyCN: 看不见时，我们就造一幅画并把它当作事实，这个动词也顺带覆盖了这种猜测。

senses.title: Used to call attention
senses.definition: used at the start of a remark to invite someone to consider something surprising
senses.definitionCN: 放在话首，请对方设想某件意外之事
senses.example: Imagine my surprise when the door opened by itself.
senses.exampleCN: 想想我当时多惊讶，门自己开了。
senses.why: Inviting a listener to picture a scene is a quick way to share a feeling, so the verb became a rhetorical opener.
senses.whyCN: 请听话人构想一个场景，是分享感受的快捷方式，于是这个动词成了修辞式的开场。

intro.en: Imagine is the French-shaped verb behind the Latin noun for picturing, and it entered English before the noun did.
intro.cn: imagine 是由拉丁语「构想」名词派生、经法语塑形的动词，进入英语的时间比名词还早。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture to oneself, a deliberate act of the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imaginari 意为在心中构想，是心智有意的动作。

items.en: The stem imagin- came from imago, a likeness or image of a thing.
items.cn: 词干 imagin- 源自 imago，即某物的形貌或影像。

items.en: French trimmed the ending to imaginer, keeping the present stem imagin-.
items.cn: 法语把词尾削为 imaginer，保留了现在时词干 imagin-。

items.en: English took it over in the fourteenth century as imaginen, now spelled imagine.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 imaginen 借用，今拼作 imagine。

items.en: The word spread from philosophy into everyday speech, where imagine now often means simply suppose.
items.cn: 这个词从哲学走入日常口语，如今常只表示「猜想」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of thinking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的各形式；近义组收其他表示思维的动词。

entries.definition: Not real, existing only in the mind; the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实、只存在于心中的形容词。

entries.definition: The faculty this verb puts to work.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词所调用的那种能力。

entries.definition: To copy, close in shape and sound but from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿，形近音近但词根不同。

entries.definition: To think something likely; plainer than imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能，比 imagine 更平实。

entries.definition: To picture something as a future possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事设想为未来的可能。

entries.definition: To form a clear picture deliberately, often for training.
entries.definitionCN: 有意形成清晰画面，常用于训练。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the verb to closed eyes, Sunday guessing and the surprise opener.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个动词系到闭上眼、周末的猜测以及惊讶的开场白上。

normal.en: Image plus -ine gives the verb; keep the root and the meaning follows.
normal.cn: image 加 -ine 就是这个动词：留住词根，意思自然跟来。

normal.en: One m, one g, then the light -ine: i-MA-gine, stress the middle.
normal.cn: 一个 m、一个 g，再接轻读的 -ine：i-MA-gine，重音在中间。

normal.en: The magic word of every exercise: imagine the scene, then describe it.
normal.cn: 所有练习的起手词：先想象场景，再来描述。

normal.en: In speech it often means simply guess, as in I imagine so.
normal.cn: 口语里常只表示「猜」，如 I imagine so。

normal.en: The g is soft, so imagine rhymes with engine and machine, not with pine.
normal.cn: g 发软音，imagine 与 engine、machine 押韵，不与 pine 同韵。

abstract.en: To imagine is to lend reality a draft copy, so the mind can try the world before it commits.
abstract.cn: 想象是给现实递上一份草稿，好让心智在定稿之前先试一试世界。

abstract.en: The word can be a question or a lantern: suppose turns it into a guess, imagine a beginning of a story.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以是疑问也可以是灯：说 suppose 时它是猜测，说 imagine 时它是故事的开头。

abstract.en: Every plan, bridge and law was once something somebody merely imagined.
abstract.cn: 每一份计划、每一座桥、每一条法律，最初都只是某人脑中的想象。

examples.en: Imagine living in a house with no windows.
examples.cn: 想象一下住在一间没有窗户的房子里。

examples.en: I imagine she will arrive before lunch.
examples.cn: 我猜她会在午饭前到。

examples.en: Try to imagine how the villagers felt that morning.
examples.cn: 试着想象那天早上村民们的心情。

dict_mnemonic.text: imag 像 + ine 动词尾——在脑中造出相似的画面，即想象

root: 拉丁语 imago（词干 imagin-）「形貌」派生动词 imaginari「在心中构想」，经古法语 imaginer 进入英语，中古英语作 imaginen。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: building a picture, guessing without proof, and inviting someone to picture a surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：造出画面、无据而猜，以及请人设想一件意外之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with closed eyes drawing shapes in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：闭着眼、在空中描画形状的人。

branches.en: THE TRAINING LINE: exercises begin with imagine the scene.
branches.cn: 训练线：练习总以「想象这个场景」开头。

branches.en: THE GUESS LINE: I imagine so replaces I suppose so.
branches.cn: 猜测线：I imagine so 可替代 I suppose so。

branches.en: THE STORY LINE: imagine opens anecdotes of surprise.
branches.cn: 故事线：imagine 用来引出令人惊讶的逸事。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: in both, the mind supplies what the eye does not.
branches.cn: 心智线：两者都是心补上眼睛没看见的。

branches.en: THE SHARING LINE: the verb invites the listener inside a picture.
branches.cn: 共享线：这个词把听者请进一幅画里。

intro.en: Imagine is the lean verb of the image family: a Latin stem and a verb ending, with cousins for every part of speech.
intro.cn: imagine 是 image 家族里最瘦的动词：拉丁词干加动词词尾，各词性都有同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb imaginari and the stem imagin- are documented, and the French -er ending replaced the Latin infinitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 imaginari 与词干 imagin- 均有文献，法语的 -er 词尾替换了拉丁不定式。

items.example: Examine and combine end the same way.
items.exampleCN: examine 与 combine 词尾相同。

items.example: Imagine a room full of clocks.
items.exampleCN: 想象一间摆满钟的房间。
他想象中的假期很安静。
他们试了所有想得到的招数。
她的想象填满了整座房子。

definition_en: happening at once, or nearest in relation, with nothing in between
core_image: 手机屏幕上跳出一条消息和一个红色的立即回复按钮
scene: 客服台前的铃声响了一声，值班的人就转身接起。The patient's illness was immediate, so there was no time to look up the file first.
sceneCN: 这里 immediate 意思是「立即的」（第 1 个义项：不隔时间的），句意是那人的病情紧急，来不及先调资料。画面里有铃响一声就转身的值班人。

pos.zh: 形容词：立即的、直接的、紧接的

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: occurring without delay, with no waiting time
senses.definitionCN: 毫无拖延、没有等待时间地发生
senses.example: The medicine brought immediate relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这药立刻缓解了症状。
senses.why: The Latin prefix means without, and the root means in between, so immediate describes a gap that simply is not there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀意为「没有」，词根意为「中间」，于是 immediate 描述的是根本不存在的间隔。

senses.title: Direct and without a middle step
senses.definition: coming from or acting on something with no intermediary
senses.definitionCN: 不经中间环节地来自或作用于某物
senses.example: Smoking is an immediate cause of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟是这种病的直接原因。
senses.why: If nothing lies between cause and result, the link is immediate, exactly as the root says.
senses.whyCN: 若因果之间不夹任何东西，这条链就是「直接」的，正是词根所说的意思。

senses.title: Nearest in place or time
senses.definition: closest in the surrounding area or in the near future
senses.definitionCN: 在周边环境或近期中最靠近的
senses.example: The immediate area was cleared for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一带被清空了两个小时。
senses.why: The nearest ring around a point has nothing between it and that point, so the same word covers physical closeness.
senses.whyCN: 围绕一点最近的圈与那点之间没有东西，于是同一个词也覆盖了空间上的近。

intro.en: Immediate is built from Latin in-, not, and mediatus, intervened, so the word literally means with nothing in between.
intro.cn: immediate 由拉丁语 in-（不）与 mediatus（介入）构成，字面意思就是「中间没有东西」。

items.en: Mediare meant to be in the middle, from medius, the word for middle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mediare 意为居间，源自 medius，即「中间的」。

items.en: Adding in- produced immediatus, describing what has nothing standing between.
items.cn: 加上 in- 构成 immediatus，形容中间不夹任何东西的状态。

items.en: Schoolmen used immediatus of the direct relation between God and the soul.
items.cn: 经院学者用 immediatus 形容神与灵魂之间的直接关系。

items.en: In philosophy the word named knowledge received without proof or medium.
items.cn: 在哲学中这个词指不经证明或媒介而得的认识。

items.en: English took immediate broadly, for instant action, direct causes and the nearest circle of people.
items.cn: 英语广泛采用，用于即时行动、直接原因与最亲近的那圈人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the medi- middle root; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is prompt.
note.cn: 形近组收带 medi-「中间」词根的词；近义组收表示迅疾的词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, meaning at once.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，意为立刻。

entries.definition: Lying in the middle, the exact opposite of having no gap.
entries.definitionCN: 居于中间的，与「无间隔」正好相反。

entries.definition: A middle thing or channel, from the same middle root.
entries.definitionCN: 中介物或媒介，同出「中间」词根。

entries.definition: Happening in a single moment, often used of products.
entries.definitionCN: 一瞬间发生的，常用于产品。

entries.definition: Done quickly and without being late.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速且不拖延地完成。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything in between.
entries.definitionCN: 中间没有人或物隔着的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks open up the literal sense: no mediator, no gap, nothing in the middle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把字面意思摊开：没有中介、没有空隙、中间没有东西。

normal.en: Im- is not, medi- is middle, so immediate is not-middle, with nothing between.
normal.cn: im- 是不，medi- 是中间，所以 immediate 就是「不隔中间」。

normal.en: Compare intermediate: add the middle and you get the opposite.
normal.cn: 对照 intermediate：加上「中间」就成了反义。

normal.en: Four beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate.
normal.cn: 四个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and becomes the word on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 成副词，就是每个应急告示上的那个词。

normal.en: Immediate family is the small circle with no relatives standing between you and them.
normal.cn: 直系亲属就是与你之间不夹旁人的那一小圈。

abstract.en: The word measures distance of a special kind: not metres, but the absence of anything in between.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量一种特殊的距离：不是米数，而是「中间空无一物」。

abstract.en: Direct causes and instant replies share one quality, the refusal of a middle step.
abstract.cn: 直接原因与即时应答共享一种性质：拒绝中间那一步。

abstract.en: Everything immediate is short-lived; the word names a moment that cannot be stored.
abstract.cn: 一切「立即」都短暂；这个词命名的是一刻无法储存的时间。

examples.en: The order takes immediate effect.
examples.cn: 该命令立即生效。

examples.en: His immediate reaction was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 他的第一反应是一言不发。

examples.en: Only the immediate family was invited to the ceremony.
examples.cn: 只有直系亲属受邀参加仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + medi 中间 + ate——中间不隔任何东西：立即的；直接的

root: 拉丁语 medius「中间」→ mediare「居间」，加否定 in- 成 immediatus，近代进入英语作 immediate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, no step in between, and no distance around.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、环节上不夹中介、空间上紧邻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flashing message with a red reply button waiting to be pressed.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上闪烁的消息和待按的红色回复键。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: immediate relief and immediate effect share a zero delay.
branches.cn: 时钟线：立刻缓解与立即生效都是零延迟。

branches.en: THE CHAIN LINE: an immediate cause needs no link before it.
branches.cn: 链条线：直接原因前面不需要再加一环。

branches.en: THE RING LINE: the immediate area and the immediate family are the closest ring.
branches.cn: 圆圈线：附近一带与直系亲属都是最内那一圈。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses depend on the same missing middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都依赖同一个「缺席的中间」。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: intermediate words do the opposite job.
branches.cn: 对照线：带 intermediate 的词正做相反的事。

intro.en: Immediate is a prefix plus a middle root plus a participle ending, a clean case of literal meaning surviving.
intro.cn: immediate 是前缀、中间词根与分词词尾的组合，字面义至今完好。

latinIntro.en: Medius and the negative in- are standard Latin, and immediatus is attested in later Latin.
latinIntro.cn: medius 与否定前缀 in- 是标准拉丁成分，immediatus 在后世拉丁文献中可见。

items.exampleCN: medium 与 mediate 共用此根。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，表示具备某性质
不隔中间，立即的、直接的

items.example: An intermediate class runs on Fridays.

items.exampleCN: 调解人与双方都见了面。

definition_en: at once, without any delay, or directly and with nothing in between
core_image: 救护车门一开，担架立刻被推进走廊
scene: 值班护士在门口听见刹车声，手上的记录本还没合上就站了起来。As soon as the bell rang, she went immediately to the ward without asking who called.
sceneCN: 这里 immediately 是「立即、马上」（第 1 个义项：毫无延迟），句意是铃一响她立刻去了病房，没问是谁按的。画面里有救护车的刹车声和还没合上的记录本。

senses.title: At once
senses.definition: in the very next moment, without waiting
senses.definitionCN: 在紧接着的一刻，不作等待
senses.example: Call the doctor immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 立刻叫医生。
senses.why: The -ly adverb keeps the literal sense of no gap and applies it to time.
senses.whyCN: 加 -ly 的副词保留「无间隔」的字面义，并把它用于时间。

senses.title: Directly, with nothing between
senses.definition: coming next in order or connected without a middle step
senses.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接，或不经中间环节地相连
senses.example: The library is immediately next to the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆就挨着礼堂。
senses.why: The same missing gap that removes waiting time also removes distance and intermediate steps.
senses.whyCN: 那个消失的间隔既能省去等待时间，也能省去距离与中间环节。

senses.title: Used for emphasis in speech
senses.definition: used to stress that someone did or refused something without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 强调某人毫不迟疑地做了或拒绝了某事
senses.example: She immediately said no to the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她一口就回绝了这个提议。
senses.why: Speech loves to mark a zero gap in reaction, and so the adverb also reports instant decisions.
senses.whyCN: 口语爱标记反应上的零间隔，因此这个副词也用来报告瞬间的决定。

intro.en: Immediately is immediate plus the Old English -lice, the ancestor of -ly.
intro.cn: immediately 是 immediate 加古英语词尾 -lice，即今日 -ly 的前身。

items.en: Immediatus already described relation without a middle term.
items.cn: 拉丁语 immediatus 已描述不带中间项的关系。

items.en: Adverbial forms like immediate stood beside the adjective in philosophical Latin.
items.cn: 在哲学拉丁语中，immediate 这类副词形式与形容词并列使用。

items.en: French used immediatement, shaping the adverb on the French pattern.
items.cn: 法语以 immediatement 的形式塑造副词。

items.en: English added its own -lice to the borrowed adjective, giving immediately.
items.cn: 英语给借来的形容词加上本土 -lice，形成 immediately。

items.en: The word became a standard instruction in medicine, law and notices.
items.cn: 这个词成了医学、法律与告示中的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and its middle-root cousins; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of haste.
note.cn: 形近组收该形容词及带「中间」词根的相关词；近义组收表示急促的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind this adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 本副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: In a middle position, the reverse of the gap being gone.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间地，与「无间隔」相反。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, often confused in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 先前地，快读时常被混淆。

entries.definition: In a single instant, often with a hint of magic.
entries.definitionCN: 一瞬间地，常带一点神奇色彩。

entries.definition: A plain phrase for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的朴素说法。

entries.definition: Without delay, common in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 不耽搁，日常口语常用。

normalIntro.en: The hooks carry the missing middle from the adjective straight into the adverb ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把形容词里那个「缺席的中间」直接带进副词词尾。

normal.en: Take immediate and add -ly; the -ly says it answers the question when.
normal.cn: 在 immediate 后加 -ly：这个词尾说明它回答「何时」。

normal.en: Five beats, stress the second: im-ME-di-ate-ly.
normal.cn: 五个拍子，重音在第二：im-ME-di-ate-ly。

normal.en: Long words can still be urgent, and this one sits on every emergency sign.
normal.cn: 长词也能万分紧急，这个词就站在每个应急告示上。

normal.en: Pair it with after or before: immediately after the meeting, immediately before dawn.
normal.cn: 常与 after 或 before 搭配：会后立即、天亮前马上。

normal.en: Not immediately obvious is the polite way of saying very hard to see.
normal.cn: not immediately obvious 是「很难看出来」的客气说法。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a gap that is not there, and in doing so it refuses every excuse of delay.
abstract.cn: 这个副词所量的是并不存在的间隙，因此它拒绝一切拖延的借口。

abstract.en: In medicine the word saves lives, and in a queue it starts quarrels.
abstract.cn: 在急诊里这个词救人，在排队时它惹人争吵。

abstract.en: Immediately is the closest English comes to naming a moment that has no length.
abstract.cn: 在英语里，immediately 最接近命名一个没有长度的瞬间。

examples.en: Please reply immediately if you receive the notice.
examples.cn: 收到通知请立即回复。

examples.en: The stairs are immediately to your left.
examples.cn: 楼梯就在你左手边。

examples.en: It was not immediately clear why the flight was delayed.
examples.cn: 航班延误的原因一时并不清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: immediate 立即的 + ly 副词尾——立即、马上；紧接地

root: immediate（拉丁语 in-「不」+ mediatus「居间」，即中间无隔）加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: no delay in time, direct connection in place or order, and emphatic instant response.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：时间上不拖延、地点或次序上直接相连，以及强调毫不迟疑的反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretcher wheeled straight down a corridor the moment the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：门一开，担架便被径直推进走廊。

branches.en: THE EMERGENCY LINE: call the doctor immediately is a life-saving instruction.
branches.cn: 急救线：「立刻叫医生」是救命的指令。

branches.en: THE MAP LINE: immediately next to marks a position with no gap.
branches.cn: 地图线：紧挨着表示不留空隙的位置。

branches.en: THE CONVERSATION LINE: immediately said no marks a decision without pause.
branches.cn: 对话线：一口回绝标记的是没有停顿的决定。

branches.en: THE GAP LINE: both senses come straight from the Latin word for middle.
branches.cn: 间隙线：两种用法都直接源自拉丁语的「中间」。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: signs and regulations use it to forbid waiting.
branches.cn: 告示线：告示与规章用它来禁止等待。

intro.en: Immediately is a Latin-derived adjective with a native adverb ending, a very common English hybrid.
intro.cn: immediately 是拉丁来源的形容词加本土副词词尾，是极常见的英式混搭。

latinIntro.en: The negative prefix and the middle root are Latin, while the -ly is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 否定前缀与「中间」词根来自拉丁语，而 -ly 属日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in a certain way or at a certain time
items.meaningCN: 副词词尾，表方式或时间
items.example: Quickly and lately both use it.
items.exampleCN: quickly 与 lately 都用它。

items.meaning: one who stands in the middle

definition_en: a strong effect on someone or something, or the force of one object hitting another
core_image: 石子落进水塘，圈纹一圈圈推到岸边
scene: 新地铁线开通三个月后，站边小店换了两轮老板。The impact on the neighbourhood was clear from the empty shops and the new coffee queue.
sceneCN: 这里 impact 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：对人或事产生的强烈作用），句意是对这一带的影响从空掉的店铺和新排起的咖啡队就能看出。画面里有地铁口的波纹状人潮。

senses.title: A strong effect
senses.definition: a powerful effect that something has on a situation or person
senses.definitionCN: 某物对局势或人产生的强烈作用
senses.example: The new policy had an impact on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策对小店产生了影响。
senses.why: The word began as physical striking and was carried over to anything that strikes a situation the way a stone strikes water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指实物的撞击，后来扩展到一切像石子击水般击中局面的东西。

senses.title: The force of a collision
senses.definition: the moment and force of one body striking another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体击中另一物体的即刻与力度
senses.example: The windscreen cracked on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 挡风玻璃一撞就裂了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, kept in physics and in accident reports.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，保留在物理学与事故报道里。

senses.title: To affect or to hit
senses.definition: to have an effect on something, or to strike it forcefully
senses.definitionCN: 对某物产生影响，或用力撞上
senses.example: Rising costs impact every household.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上涨冲击着每一个家庭。
senses.why: English turns almost any strong noun into a verb, and impact took that route in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 英语几乎能把任何强势名词变动词，impact 在二十世纪就走上了这条路。

intro.en: Impact began as a Latin participle meaning driven in or pressed against, and only later became a noun for effect.
intro.cn: impact 最初是拉丁语分词，意为「打入、压向」，后来才成为表示「影响」的名词。

items.en: Pangere meant to fasten or strike, and its participle pactus described something fixed or driven in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pangere 意为固定或击打，其分词 pactus 描述被钉入或压紧之物。

items.en: Impactus was the strengthened form, pressed hard against something.
items.cn: impactus 是加强形式，意为被重重压向某物。

items.en: English took impact in the seventeenth century as a term in mechanics for collision.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪以力学用语的「碰撞」义引入 impact。

items.en: In the twentieth century it broadened into the general sense of a strong effect.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，它扩展为泛指强烈影响。

items.en: Verb use grew after the 1950s and is now common in business writing.
items.cn: 动词用法在1950年代后增多，如今在商务写作中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same pacting root; the near-meaning group gathers words for effect.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「钉入、击打」词根的词；近义组收表示作用的词。

entries.definition: An agreement fixed between parties, from the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 各方订立的约定，同根。

entries.definition: Pressed closely together, sharing the fastening root.
entries.definitionCN: 紧压在一起的，同出「紧固」之根。

entries.definition: The state of being wedged or pressed in, especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 被卡住压紧的状态，多用于医学。

entries.definition: A result caused by something; quieter than impact.
entries.definitionCN: 由某物引起的结果，语气比 impact 平。

entries.definition: The power to change how someone acts or thinks.
entries.definitionCN: 改变他人行为或想法的力量。

entries.definition: The physical crashing of two objects, close to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 两个物体的实体相撞，接近第二个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the Latin fastening root to ripples on a pond and to business verb use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁「钉紧」词根连到水塘涟漪与商务动词用法上。

normal.en: The root pact means fixed together, as in a peace pact; impact is a blow that fixes a mark.
normal.cn: 词根 pact 意为固定在一起，如和平协定；impact 是留下痕迹的击打。

normal.en: Noun stress first: IM-pact; verb often the same in modern English.
normal.cn: 名词重音在前：IM-pact；现代英语动词常同音。

normal.en: Have an impact on is the safest phrase: preposition on, not for.
normal.cn: 最稳的搭配是 have an impact on，介词用 on。

normal.en: On impact is the expression in crash reports.
normal.cn: 事故报道里用 on impact 表示「撞击时」。

normal.en: A stone, a policy and a rumour can all make the same ripples.
normal.cn: 石子、政策与谣言都能激起同样的涟漪。

abstract.en: The word began with bodies meeting and ended with lives meeting, and the physics stayed.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于物体相遇，终于人生相遇，而那点物理学一直留着。

abstract.en: Impact measures what something leaves behind, so every use implies a before and an after.
abstract.cn: impact 衡量某物留下了什么，因此每次使用都隐含一个之前与一个之后。

abstract.en: A policy with no impact has failed quietly, and a person with impact has changed the room on entering.
abstract.cn: 毫无影响的政策是悄悄失败了，而有影响力的人一进屋就改变了房间。

examples.en: The report examines the impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 这份报告考察旅游业对海岸的影响。

examples.en: The car hit the barrier and the driver was thrown forward on impact.
examples.cn: 汽车撞上护栏，撞击时司机被向前抛出。

examples.en: Rising fuel prices impacted the whole industry.
examples.cn: 燃料涨价冲击了整个行业。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + pact 压紧（如 pact 协定）——狠狠压进去，即撞击；引申为冲击、影响

root: 拉丁语 pangere「钉入、击打」→ 分词 impactus「被压向的」，十七世纪进入英语作力学用语，二十世纪扩展为「影响」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a strong effect, a physical collision, and the verb made from both.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强烈影响、实体撞击，以及由两者转来的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples from a dropped stone reaching the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：石子落水后，涟漪一直推到岸边。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: the word asks what changed after the decision.
branches.cn: 政策线：这个词问的是决定之后改变了什么。

branches.en: THE ACCIDENT LINE: on impact reports the instant of collision.
branches.cn: 事故线：on impact 报告相撞的一瞬。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS LINE: impact as a verb suits reports and meetings.
branches.cn: 商务线：impact 作动词适合理报告与开会。

branches.en: THE FORCE LINE: both senses carry a sense of something arriving hard.
branches.cn: 力量线：两种用法都带着「重重抵达」之感。

branches.en: THE RIPPLE LINE: the noun and verb name cause and consequence.
branches.cn: 涟漪线：名词与动词分别命名起因与后果。

intro.en: Impact is a Latin participle used as a noun, with a small modern family including a back-formed verb.
intro.cn: impact 是当作名词用的拉丁分词，现代又反向造出动词，形成一个小家族。

latinIntro.en: Pangere and impactus are recorded in Latin, and pact- supplies the fixed-agreement branch of the family.
latinIntro.cn: pangere 与 impactus 均有拉丁文献，pact- 这一支则长出「订约」的意义。

items.example: Import carries a similar inward sense.
items.exampleCN: import 也有类似的向内感。

items.example: The impact was felt for years.
The area was badly impacted by the flood.
items.exampleCN: 这一带受洪水影响严重。
他们想要一个有力的开场。

items.example: The two sides signed a pact.

definition_zh: 实施；执行；贯彻；（名词）工具、器具
definition_en: to put a plan or decision into effect, or a tool used for a particular job
core_image: 钉在车间墙上的新流程图，旁边挂着一把扳手
scene: 新规定贴在门口，第二周真的开始执行了。Once the manager decided to implement the safety rules, every worker had to sign the sheet before entering.
sceneCN: 这里 implement 是「实施、执行」（第 1 个义项：把计划变为实际做法），句意是经理一旦决定实施安全规定，每个工人进门前都要在表上签到。画面里有门口贴的新规定和墙上的流程图。

derivatives.zh: （形近）作为工具或手段的、辅助实施的

senses.title: To carry a plan into effect
senses.definition: to take a decision, rule or plan and make it work in practice
senses.definitionCN: 把决定、规定或计划真正落实为做法
senses.example: The school will implement the new timetable in March.
senses.exampleCN: 学校将在三月实施新的课表。
senses.why: The Latin root means to fill up, and carrying out a plan fills the gap between intention and fact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「填满」，而落实计划正是把「打算」与「事实」之间的空隙填满。

senses.title: A tool for a task
senses.definition: an object used to carry out a particular kind of work
senses.definitionCN: 用于完成某类工作的物件
senses.example: Old farm implements hang in the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓里挂着旧农具。
senses.why: A tool is what supplies a job with what it needs, so the filling root named the thing that fills the lack.
senses.whyCN: 工具正是为工作补上所缺之物，因此那个表示「填满」的词根也命名了补缺的物件。

senses.title: To put into practice as a duty
senses.definition: used of officials whose job is to make rules real
senses.definitionCN: 用于负责把规则落到实处的人员
senses.example: Inspectors must implement the standards without favour.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员必须不偏不倚地贯彻这些标准。
senses.why: When an institution delegates execution, the verb takes an official subject and gains a tone of duty.
senses.whyCN: 当机构把执行权委派下去时，这个动词的主语多为官方人员，语气带上职责感。

intro.en: Implement is built on a Latin verb meaning to fill up, and both tool and execution grow from that idea of supplying what is missing.
intro.cn: implement 建立在拉丁语「填满」动词之上，工具与执行两种用法都从「补上所缺」这一想法长出。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and its root sits inside plenus, full.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plere 意为填满，其词根也藏在 plenus（满的）之中。

items.en: Implere meant to fill up completely, to complete what was lacking.
items.cn: implere 意为彻底填满，把所缺的部分补齐。

items.en: Its participle impletum, with the noun implementum, named a filling and later a thing that fills a need.
items.cn: 其分词 impletum 与名词 implementum 指充填，后指满足需要的物件。

items.en: English took implement as a noun for equipment in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语以名词形式引入 implement，指装备器具。

items.en: The verb came much later, and in the twentieth century business and government made implement a standard word for carrying out policy.
items.cn: 动词用法出现得晚得多，二十世纪企业与政府把 implement 变成「执行政策」的标准词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the filling root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of carrying out.
note.cn: 形近组收「填满」词根的词；近义组收表示执行的动词。

entries.definition: The act of putting a plan into practice.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划付诸实行的行为。

entries.definition: Something that completes another, from the same filling root.
entries.definitionCN: 补足另一物之物，同出「填满」之根。

entries.definition: Fully filled, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 完全填满、一无所缺的。

entries.definition: To do what was planned, in plain everyday words.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划好的事做出来，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To perform a plan or order, often with legal or military weight.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划或命令，常带法律或军事语气。

entries.definition: To put a rule or method to practical use.
entries.definitionCN: 把规则或方法用到实际中。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the filling root to a wrench on the wall and to a policy that must reach the shop floor.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「填满」词根连到墙上的扳手和必须落到车间的政策上。

normal.en: Im- in, ple- fill: implement is to fill the plan in with action.
normal.cn: im- 向内，ple- 填满：implement 就是把行动填进计划里。

normal.en: The verb stresses the first syllable in British English: IM-ple-ment.
normal.cn: 英式英语里动词重音在前：IM-ple-ment。

normal.en: Noun and verb share a spelling, unlike complement with an e.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，注意别与带 e 的 complement 混淆。

normal.en: A tool is what fills your hand with what the job needs.
normal.cn: 工具就是把干活所需之物填进你手里的东西。

normal.en: Policies are written in offices but implemented in shops and schools.
normal.cn: 政策写在办公室里，却是实施在店铺与学校里。

abstract.en: The word names the hardest half of any reform, the part after the announcement.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是一切改革中最难的那一半，即宣布之后的部分。

abstract.en: Its two senses meet in one idea: something missing gets supplied, by a hand tool or by a bureaucrat.
abstract.cn: 两个义项在一个想法里相遇：缺什么补什么，或用手里的工具，或用公职人员。

abstract.en: A good plan unimplemented is only a hope written down.
abstract.cn: 未能落地的良策，只是写下来的愿望。

examples.en: The government promised to implement the report's advice.
examples.cn: 政府承诺落实报告中的建议。

examples.en: Implementing the change took three months of training.
examples.cn: 实施这项变动花了三个月培训。

examples.en: Simple stone implements were found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞中发现了简单的石制器具。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 使 + ple 填满 + ment 名词/动词尾——把空缺填满：实施；能补上所需之物的工具

root: 拉丁语 implere「填满」→ 分词 impletum、名词 implementum，十五世纪进入英语作名词「器具」，二十世纪衍生动词「实施」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: carrying out a plan, the tool used for work, and the official duty of making rules real.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：落实计划、干活用的工具，以及把规定真正落地的职务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a policy poster on a factory door beside a wrench hanging on a nail.
core.cn: 核心意象：车间门口的政策告示，旁边的钉子上挂着一把扳手。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: timetables and rules turn into actions.
branches.cn: 办公室线：课表与规定变成实际行动。

branches.en: THE BARN LINE: implements hang where farm work happens.
branches.cn: 谷仓线：农具挂在真正做农活的地方。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: inspectors implement standards without favour.
branches.cn: 职责线：检查员不偏不倚地贯彻标准。

branches.en: THE HANDS LINE: tools fill the hands, plans fill the calendar.
branches.cn: 手边线：工具填满双手，计划填满日程。

branches.en: THE FOLLOW-UP LINE: both name the work that comes after the decision.
branches.cn: 后续线：两者指的都是决定之后的活儿。

intro.en: Implement is a Latin filling verb turned English noun and then verb again, with a family of completion words.
intro.cn: implement 是拉丁语「填满」动词先变英语名词、再变动词，身边是一族「完备」词。

latinIntro.en: Plere and implere are recorded in Latin, and the participle supplies the English stem.
latinIntro.cn: plere 与 implere 均有拉丁文献，其分词提供了英语词干。

items.meaningCN: 表示物或结果的名词词尾

items.meaning: a tool; to put into effect
items.example: They implemented the plan at once.
The scheme was implemented last year.

items.meaning: the carrying out of a plan
something added to fill a lack

latinEntries.meaning: a filling, a means of filling

definition_en: a meaning suggested but not stated, or a likely result that follows from something
core_image: 一句话说完后，听者脸上瞬间的迟疑
scene: 会上经理说预算「不会更少」，没人笑。The implication was that someone would be let go, though nobody had said so.
sceneCN: 这里 implication 是「暗示、言外之意」（第 1 个义项：未明说而蕴含的意思），句意是言外之意是有人要走，尽管没人说出来。画面里有迟疑的听者和会议室。

pos.zh: 名词：含义、暗示、言外之意；影响、后果；牵连

senses.title: A meaning not stated
senses.definition: an idea that the speaker or writer suggests without saying it directly
senses.definitionCN: 说者或作者未明说却暗示的意思
senses.example: The implication of his remark was clear to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句话的言外之意人人都懂。
senses.why: The Latin root means folded in, and a hinted meaning is folded inside the words rather than laid out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「折进里面」，被暗示的意思正是折在话语之内，而未摊开。

senses.title: A likely result
senses.definition: a consequence that a decision or fact is likely to bring
senses.definitionCN: 某项决定或事实很可能带来的后果
senses.example: The finding has implications for food safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现对食品安全有影响。
senses.why: A consequence is also folded inside a cause, waiting to unfold, so the same noun covers results.
senses.whyCN: 后果同样折在原因之内、等着被展开，于是同一个名词也涵盖结果。

senses.title: Involvement in wrongdoing
senses.definition: the fact of being involved in a crime or a scandal
senses.definitionCN: 卷入罪行或丑闻的事实
senses.example: His implication in the fraud ended his career.
senses.exampleCN: 他牵连进这起诈骗案，就此断送了事业。
senses.why: To be folded into an affair is exactly what involvement means, so the noun also reports guilt by association.
senses.whyCN: 被折进一桩事件，正是「牵连」，因此这个名词也用来报告「因关联而有嫌疑」。

intro.en: Implication is the Latin noun of folding in, and that physical image survives in every modern sense.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语的「折入」名词，这个具体意象在每种现代用法中都还活着。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and the fold could be cloth, a letter or an argument.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，可折的是布、信，也可是一套论证。

items.en: Implicare folded something into something else, and hence entangled it.
items.cn: implicare 指把一物折进另一物，因而也指卷入、缠上。

items.en: Implicatio named that entanglement or the act of folding in.
items.cn: implicatio 命名这种缠绕，或折入的动作。

items.en: French used implication for involvement and for meaning carried within words.
items.cn: 法语用 implication 表示卷入，也指话语内含的意思。

items.en: Logic gave English the sense of what follows from a statement, now the commonest use.
items.cn: 逻辑学赋予英语「由陈述推出什么」这一义，如今是最常见的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fold family; the near-meaning group gathers words for hinted meaning and consequence.
note.cn: 形近组收「折叠」词族；近义组收表示暗示与后果的词。

entries.definition: To suggest without stating, the verb behind this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不说明而暗示，本名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Folded in, not openly expressed.
entries.definitionCN: 折在其中的、不显明表达的。

entries.definition: A difficulty folded together with the main matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与主要事情绞在一起的麻烦。

entries.definition: A result that follows, closer to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 随之而来的结果，接近第二个义项。

entries.definition: A hint or idea put forward softly.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻提出的暗示或想法。

entries.definition: Being mixed up in an affair, close to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 卷入某事件，接近第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the folding image, which explains hidden meaning, hidden results and hidden guilt.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用「折」这个意象，它同时解释了隐义、隐果与隐罪。

normal.en: Plic means fold, so implication is what is folded inside a sentence.
normal.cn: plic 意为折，implication 就是折进句子里的东西。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: im-pli-CA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第三音节：im-pli-CA-tion。

normal.en: The verb is imply, the adjective implicit: all three wear the same fold.
normal.cn: 动词是 imply，形容词是 implicit，三者都带着同一个「折」。

normal.en: By implication is a useful phrase for reading between the lines.
normal.cn: by implication 是「读出弦外之音」的好用短语。

normal.en: Have implications for keeps the preposition for, not on.
normal.cn: have implications for 的介词是 for，不是 on。

abstract.en: A fold hides a surface and preserves it at once, which is why the word can mean both a secret meaning and a stored result.
abstract.cn: 折叠既藏起一面又保存它，所以这个词既能指隐藏的意思，也能指被存下的结果。

abstract.en: What is implied is present and absent at the same time, like an object under a cloth.
abstract.cn: 被暗示之物既在场又不在场，像布下的一件东西。

abstract.en: Arguments often move by implication, and the honest reader keeps unfolding the cloth.
abstract.cn: 论证常靠暗示推进，诚实的读者会不断把布展开。

examples.en: He objected to the implication that he had been careless.
examples.cn: 他反对那种暗示他不小心的说法。

examples.en: The new law has implications for every landlord.
examples.cn: 新法律对每个房东都有影响。

examples.en: She denied any implication in the scheme.
examples.cn: 她否认与这个计划有任何牵连。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + plic 折 + ation 名词——折进话里的意思：言外之意；折进事里的结果：影响

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」→ implicare「折入、卷入」→ implicatio，经古法语 implication 进入英语，逻辑学使其定指「蕴含之义」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a hinted meaning, a likely consequence, and involvement in a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：暗示的意思、可能的后果，以及被卷进某桩事情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pause on the listeners' faces after a sentence ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：话说完后，听者脸上那一瞬的停顿。

branches.en: THE MEETING LINE: the implication is that signals bad news.
branches.cn: 会议线：the implication is that 常引出坏消息。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: implications for whole industries.
branches.cn: 政策线：对整行业的影响。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: implication in a fraud ends careers.
branches.cn: 法庭线：牵连进诈骗会断送前程。

branches.en: THE FOLD LINE: a hint and a result are both folded inside something.
branches.cn: 折叠线：暗示与结果都折在某物之内。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE LINE: both senses report what follows from an act.
branches.cn: 后果线：两种用法都报告某种行为之后跟着来的东西。

intro.en: Implication is a Latin fold plus the noun ending -ation, in a family that includes imply and implicit.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语「折」加名词词尾 -ation，同族有 imply 与 implicit。

latinIntro.en: Plicare, implicare and implicatio are all recorded in Latin, so the folding image is documented.
latinIntro.cn: plicare、implicare 与 implicatio 在拉丁语中均有文献，「折」的意象有据。

items.example: The root also appears in complicate.

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.example: Are you implying that I lied?
There is an implicit warning in the letter.

definition_en: to suggest something without saying it directly, or to be a natural sign of something
core_image: 说话人眼神扫过空椅子，然后停在门口
scene: 介绍人没提任何名字，只说了句「位置还空着」。By saying the seat was empty, she implied that one of them was leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 imply 是「暗示」（第 1 个义项：不明说而让人领会），句意是她说座位空着，等于暗示其中一人要离开。画面里有扫过空椅子的眼神。

pos.zh: 动词：暗示、意味着、含有……的意思

senses.title: To suggest without saying
senses.definition: to make a listener understand something that is not spoken out
senses.definitionCN: 使听者领会未被说出的意思
senses.example: I did not mean to imply that you were wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 我并不想暗示你错了。
senses.why: The fold inside the Latin root explains it: the meaning is folded in, waiting to be opened by the listener.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根里的「折」正好解释：意思被折进去，等听者去展开。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: used of facts which logically point to a further fact
senses.definitionCN: 用于事实在逻辑上指向另一事实的情况
senses.example: The empty shelves imply a shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的货架意味着短缺。
senses.why: Things imply each other as well as people, when one fact cannot stand without another behind it.
senses.whyCN: 不仅人，事物之间也互相蕴含：当一个事实离开背后的事实便站不住时。

senses.title: To involve as a necessary part
senses.definition: to bring something with it as a necessary condition
senses.definitionCN: 必然附带某条件或结果
senses.example: Taking the job implies moving to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 接下这份工作就意味着搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: A consequence folded into an action is implied by that action, so the verb also marks necessary conditions.
senses.whyCN: 折在行动里的后果由该行动所蕴含，于是这个动词也标示必要条件。

intro.en: Imply comes from the Latin verb for folding in, and English shaped it through French implication.
intro.cn: imply 来自拉丁语「折入」动词，英语形式经法语影响而定形。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and implicare to fold one thing into another.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，implicare 指把一物折进另一物。

items.en: French used emplier and later implied forms for wrapping a meaning inside words.
items.cn: 法语以 emplier 及后来的 implied 形式表示把含义包进言语。

items.en: English formed imply in the fourteenth century on the French model.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪仿法语模式造出 imply。

items.en: Logic gave the verb its technical sense: one statement implies another.
items.cn: 逻辑学赋予它专业义：一个陈述蕴含另一个陈述。

items.en: Everyday speech uses it constantly for polite hints and gentle accusations.
items.cn: 日常口语中它大量用于客气的暗示与委婉的指责。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fold family; the near-meaning group separates the confusable suggesting verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收「折叠」词族；近义组分辨几个容易混淆的「提示」动词。

entries.definition: The hinted meaning itself, as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 被暗示的意思本身，名词形式。

entries.definition: Folded in, understood without being stated.
entries.definitionCN: 折在其中、不待明说的。

entries.definition: To put to use, shaped like imply but from a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 应用、申请，形式与 imply 相似但前缀不同。

entries.definition: What the listener does with a hint, while imply is what the speaker does.
entries.definitionCN: 听者从暗示中推出；imply 是说着做的，infer 是听者做的。

entries.definition: To put an idea forward softly; wider than imply.
entries.definitionCN: 柔和地提出想法，比 imply 范围更广。

entries.definition: To have as a meaning, the plainest word in the group.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「意思是」，这组里最朴素的词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks pair imply with infer, and unfold the fold image into a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 imply 与 infer 配成一对，并把「折」的意象展开进句子里。

normal.en: The speaker implies, the listener infers; keep the direction straight.
normal.cn: 说者 imply，听者 infer，方向不能颠倒。

normal.en: Drop the e before -ed and -es: implied, implies.
normal.cn: -ed 与 -es 前要省掉 e：implied、implies。

normal.en: Two beats, stress the second: im-PLY.
normal.cn: 两个音节，重音在后：im-PLY。

normal.en: The plic fold hides inside, so the meaning is never on the surface.
normal.cn: '折'藏在里面，所以意思从不在表面上。

normal.en: As the name implies is a fixture of explanations and manuals.
normal.cn: as the name implies 是解释与手册里的常客。

abstract.en: The verb respects what silence can carry, since it lets a speaker act without saying.
abstract.cn: 这个动词尊重沉默所能承载的东西，让说者不必开口也能行动。

abstract.en: Facts imply too, and a good reader treats the world as a text folded in layers.
abstract.cn: 事实也会蕴含，好的读者把世界当作层层折叠的文本。

abstract.en: Accusations often travel through imply because it leaves no fingerprints.
abstract.cn: 指责常借 imply 传递，因为它不留指纹。

examples.en: The letter implies that the contract will not be renewed.
examples.cn: 这封信意味着合同不会续签。

examples.en: Are you implying that I made the mistake?
examples.cn: 你是在暗示是我的错吗？

examples.en: Silence does not imply agreement.
examples.cn: 沉默并不意味着同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + ply 折（plic 的变体）——把意思折进话里，不明说：暗示

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」→ implicare「折入」，经法语影响，英语十四世纪造出 imply。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a polite hint, a sign in facts, and a necessary consequence.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：委婉的暗示、事实上的迹象，以及必然伴随的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker's glance at an empty chair, then at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人瞥向空椅，又看向门口。

branches.en: THE HINT LINE: I did not mean to imply that is a common repair phrase.
branches.cn: 暗示线：我无意暗示……是常见的补救话。

branches.en: THE CLUE LINE: empty shelves imply shortage.
branches.cn: 线索线：空货架意味着短缺。

branches.en: THE CONDITION LINE: a job implies moving.
branches.cn: 条件线：一份工作意味着搬迁。

branches.en: THE PARTNER LINE: imply needs an inferring mind at the other end.
branches.cn: 搭档线：imply 需要另一端有一个在推断的心。

branches.en: THE LOGIC LINE: both are about what must follow.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：两者都关乎必然跟着来的东西。

intro.en: Imply is the verb of the fold family, with a dropped letter in its past forms and a noun in -ation.
intro.cn: imply 是「折叠」家族的动词，过去形式要省字母，名词以 -ation 收尾。

latinIntro.en: Implicare is Latin; the English verb was reshaped through French spelling habits.
latinIntro.cn: implicare 属拉丁语；英语动词形式受法语拼写习惯重塑。

items.example: Import begins with the same prefix.
Reply and apply use the same shape.
items.exampleCN: reply 与 apply 形式相近。
这一结果意味着更多工作。
这名字意味着年头很久。

items.example: She implied nothing of the kind.
He was implying more than he said.

items.exampleCN: 规则里明确写了这一点。

definition_zh: 进口；引进；输入；（名词）进口品
definition_en: to bring goods into a country from abroad, or goods brought in this way
core_image: 码头上一排排从船腹里吊出来的集装箱
scene: 港口每天清早最忙，吊车一刻不停。The country imports most of its oil, so every delay on the shipping route is felt at the pumps.
sceneCN: 这里 import 是「进口」（第 1 个义项：把货物从国外运入本国），句意是这个国家的石油大多靠进口，因此航线上任何延误都会在加油站被感受到。画面里有码头上被吊起的集装箱。

collocations.zh: 这一信息的分量（引申义）

senses.title: To bring goods in from abroad
senses.definition: to buy and bring goods into one's own country
senses.definitionCN: 从国外购入并把货物运入本国
senses.example: The factory imports steel from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂从三个国家进口钢材。
senses.why: The prefix means into and the root means carry, so import is literally to carry in.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「向内」，词根意为「搬运」，所以 import 字面就是「向内搬运」。

senses.title: A good brought in
senses.definition: the goods or services brought into a country this way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种方式进入本国的货物或服务
senses.example: Imports rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年进口额大幅上升。
senses.why: The action and its object share one form in English, so the noun simply names what the verb brings.
senses.whyCN: 英语里动作与对象常共用一个形式，名词就直接指动词带进来的东西。

senses.title: The meaning or weight of words
senses.definition: the significance carried by a statement or event, a formal use
senses.definitionCN: 言语或事件所承载的意义，属正式用法
senses.example: Few understood the import of his words.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人听懂他话里的分量。
senses.why: To carry is not only to move boxes; words and events carry meaning, and the old verb kept that freight sense.
senses.whyCN: 搬运不只运箱子，词与事件也承载意义，这个旧动词保留了这份「载重」之意。

intro.en: Import is a Latin verb for carrying in, and its shipping sense has survived unchanged for centuries.
intro.cn: import 是拉丁语「搬入」动词，其航运本义历经数百年未变。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and importare meant to carry in or bring in.
items.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，importare 意为搬入、带入。

items.en: Trade Latin used importare for bringing goods into a province or a city.
items.cn: 商业用的拉丁语以 importare 指把货物运入行省或城市。

items.en: English took import at first for bringing in goods, and also for bringing in ideas.
items.cn: 英语最初用 import 指运入货物，也指引入观念。

items.en: Nation states and customs houses made import a fixed term of trade and duty.
items.cn: 民族国家与海关把 import 定为贸易与关税的固定术语。

items.en: The formal sense of weight or meaning kept the old freight metaphor alive.
items.cn: 表示「分量、含义」的正式用法让古老的「载重」比喻得以延续。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers carry-root words; the near-meaning group gathers trade words and their opposites.
note.cn: 形近组收「搬运」词根的词；近义组收贸易词及其对立词。

entries.definition: To carry goods out, the exact mirror of import.
entries.definitionCN: 把货运出去，正是 import 的镜像。

entries.definition: Easy to carry, from the same carrying root.
entries.definitionCN: 便于携带的，同出「搬运」之根。

entries.definition: Of great weight, built on the same freight idea.
entries.definitionCN: 很有分量的，同出「载重」之意。

entries.definition: The plain everyday phrase for importing.
entries.definitionCN: 进口的朴素日常说法。

entries.definition: To bring something in for the first time, often ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 首次引进，多指观念。

entries.definition: A load of goods sent, whether in or out.
